description.narrative: To extend institutional strengthening support to the National Ozone Unit (NOU) of the Department of Environment to provide the requisite resources and capacity for continued implementation of Montreal Protocol operational activities.

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

comment.narrative:
1. On-going ODS phase-out and control & monitoring activities by the NOU for compliance to the Montreal Protocol
2. On-going awareness programmes for the Montreal Protocol (including the Kigali Amendment) and related amendments and gazettements of EQA regulation
3. Continued operation of the Programme Management Unit (PMU) of the NOU

1. Support capacity of National Ozone Unit to participate in Montreal Protocol meetings and to achieve objectives and targets of the national HPMP-II programme
2. Support capacity of the National Ozone Unit to hold awareness programmes and capacity building sessions related to the implementation of activities under the Montreal Protocol
3. Provide resources to maintain capacity of the PMU

1. NOU participated in 8 international meetings/conferences related to the Montreal Protocol (virtually), in addition to developing progress in the HPMP-II programme.
2. Continued control of import & export of ODS substances in cooperation with the national Customs department and relevant agencies, where DOE processed and approved 1143 permits for (HCFC, HFC and Halon 1301) and visited 3 registered importers premises to verify declared stock.
3. NOU held 1 Project Steering Committee (PSC) meeting in January, and conducted 10 awareness/capacity building programmes nationwide for various stakeholder groups
4. The IS project provided funding resources for the sustained operations of the NOU which includes the hiring of 4 contract staff as well as contributions to the DOE Trust Fund.
5. Successful ratification of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol on 21 October 2020, which will lead to the overall reduction of HFC substances in contribution towards Malaysias carbon and climate change mitigation measures.
6. ODS Data Verification with relevant agencies such as Department of Statistics Malaysia, Department of Agriculture Malaysia (on Methyl Bromide) and Royal Malaysian Customs Department for timely reporting of A7 data to the Ozone Secretariat. National ODS consumption level in 2019 = 214.21 ODP tonnes (below the allowable limit of 400 ODP tonnes)
